2abc6b757313f2b4c868fa2c960b7a06d7cab880.summary: KSI Digital analyses 'Ancient', a Linux IoT botnet family captured in its SSH/Telnet honeypot between 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-05. Delivery was a Telnet login by an already-infected device, followed by a shell dropper that went through three versions. The bot hides its C2 lookup via DNS-over-TLS and stays dormant while traced. A 10-minute controlled contact confirmed the C2 was live. Its C2 protocol is a custom handshake tagged ANCT, not Mirai's, though some feeds label its binaries Mirai. The same loader tooling delivered an unrelated Mirai kit a day later from a shared network. Whether one…

hedges: The bot appears to stay idle while being ptraced.
The 32-byte client message is consistent with a key exchange (consistent with a key exchange); the report does not confirm it.
The ANCT tag reads as an abbreviation of 'ANCienT', matching the dropper's naming.
It looks like a generic loader routine whose first line was changed to a campaign-specific marker.
Either the server kept handing out an older build or the operator rolled back.
That fits one operator running both, or a shared loader service with several customers. We can't tell which from our data.
The key exchange and cipher behind the ANCT handshake are open questions; the bot's upload content is unknown.
